topic.title: Table: which datasets, data and models can be used (host answers)
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
I summarized which datasets, data and models can be used, in a table. Each row quotes the host's reply in the linked thread.

Dataset / data / model Can use? Host reply Thread
train.parquet and models trained on it Yes "can be treated effectively as open-source and any model trained on it is fine, redistributed artifacts are fine" 745841
Datasets that are non-commercial only because they come from train.parquet Yes "any datasets that are only noncommercial by inheriting from train.parquet are fine to use" 745072
MassSpecGym and models trained on it Yes "we consider MassSpecGym and models trained on it and released with permissive licenses as fair game" 742991
GLACIER / ICEBERG (MassSpecGym-trained) Yes "MassSpecGym is allowed, so is GLACIER" / "GLACIER/ICEBERG, DreaMS and ChEBI/LIPID MAPS are all fine" 744338, 745841
DreaMS Yes "DreaMS weights are allowed" 745604
ChEBI / LIPID MAPS Yes "GLACIER/ICEBERG, DreaMS and ChEBI/LIPID MAPS are all fine" 745841
CFM-ID 4 Yes "CFM ID 4 is fine" 743774
Newer GNPS / MassBank / MoNA releases Yes "Newer releases of public datasets are fine to use and CC BY-SA records are acceptable" 745228
GNPS-NIST14-MATCHES Yes "Allowed for library matching and training" 745832
Enveda-180 Zenodo release Yes "Data in the Zenodo release of Enveda-180 are fine to use" 745148
PubChem Yes "PubChem structures for retrieval are acceptable" / "submitting subsets of PubChem is fine" 741857
COCONUT Yes "the large molecule libraries like PubChem and COCONUT that are generally treated as open source" are fine 745072
NIST (and models trained on it) No "any solution using or trained on NIST will be disqualified" 744470
Newly created NIST-derived datasets No "NIST would consider any newly created such datasets to be derivatives and in violation of their license" 745832
